items.title: Senate is still a toss-up, but Democrats now have slight edge, prediction market traders think
items.summary: The battle for the U.S. Senate is still tight, but prediction market traders think Democrats have close to their best chances yet of taking the upper chamber.

items.title: China's AI leaders keep quiet despite U.S. 'publicity' on tech risks
items.summary: BEIJING — While frontier U.S. labs have sounded the alarm on artificial intelligence in recent high-profile speeches, Chinese companies have largely kept quiet.

items.summary: Transportation companies, the lifeblood of the U.S. economy , are flashing warning signs as diesel costs hit records.

items.title: Consumers hit by one-two punch of oil and rates from Iran war. The estimated bill is $1,700 per household
items.summary: Consumers are facing a double-whammy of jumping oil prices and Treasury yields amid the U.S. war with Iran that is leaving them increasingly cash-strapped.

items.title: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar
items.summary: The U.K.'s annual inflation rate jumped to 3.1% in August, pushed up by surging gasoline and diesel prices.

items.title: Indonesia's new finance minister faces an uphill battle on fiscal credibility
items.summary: Indonesia just got its third third finance minister in two years, putting the spotlight on concerns plaguing Southeast Asia's largest economy , with analysts flagging the need for fiscal prudence and a shift away from "interventionist" policy.

items.title: Why de-dollarization discussions are more talk, less action
items.summary: When BRICS leaders met over the weekend, they talked about the economic power of the Global South and the need to expand trade in local currencies, signaling a push to cut dependence on the greenback.
